findings.body: The link color changes from scale-color($primary, 50%... originally 30%) to 70%, producing a near-white, low-contrast, barely readable username link on light themes; the dark-theme value also deviates from the (100% - lightness) complement convention used by every other conversion in this patch (30% -> 70%).
findings.failure_mode: Visual regression: topic author name links become nearly invisible on light color schemes, unlike all sibling conversions which preserve the original light-theme color.
findings.impact: The link color changes from scale-color($primary, 50%... originally 30%) to 70%, producing a near-white, low-contrast, barely readable username link on light themes; the dark-theme value also deviates from the (100% - lightness) complement convention used by every other conversion in this patch (30% -> 70%).
findings.root_cause: The mechanical scale-color -> dark-light-choose conversion swapped the lightness percentages: the original 30% light-theme value was replaced with 70% and the dark-theme complement 70% was replaced with 30%.
findings.suggested_fix: Use dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)) to preserve the original light-theme value and follow the complement convention for dark themes.
findings.title: Light-theme color regressed and arguments inverted for .topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.trigger: Render any topic post with a light color scheme (default: $primary #222 on $secondary #fff) and view the poster name link in .topic-meta-data h5.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch confirms L291 changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The light-theme value changed from 30% to 70%, which is inverted - lighter text on light backgrounds reduces contrast. The claim is accurate and grounded in the diff.

findings.suggested_fix: Change to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) to preserve the original light-theme value and match desktop/modal.scss.
